text:
Casey: Hey @Jordan — Epoch Health is ready to start their 2-week POC. They want a hosted API key but security requires automatic rotation, IP allowlist, and revocation when the POC ends. Can we get an operational plan?

Jordan: Yes. We usually provide ephemeral hosted keys for POCs. Do we know the TTL they need and the IP ranges?

Casey: Customer prefers 48h TTL, but security asked if we can rotate every 24h. IPs are 198.51.100.23/32 and 2001:db8::/64. Also they want an audit trail of rotations.

Priya: We can support that. Two options:
- Console-created ephemeral key with manual rotation, or
- API-driven ephemeral key + rotation job + webhook to vault for key updates (recommended for automation).

Priya: Example create call (internal poc-keys endpoint):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/internal/poc-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $INTERNAL_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project":"epoch-poc","ttl":"48h","ip_allowlist":["198.51.100.23/32","2001:db8::/64"],"rotate_every":"24h","notify":"vault://redwood/pocs/epoch"}'
```
Response returns key_id and the initial token (token only shown once).

Priya: For rotation we recommend a small cron job in our infra account that calls:
```
POST /v1/internal/poc-keys/<key_id>/rotate
{ "rotate_to_ttl": "48h" }
```
and on success it writes the new token to the vault path you provided. That satisfies audit + no plaintext in email.

Lena: Security checks — please ensure:
- Rotated tokens are written to customer-specific KMS-backed vault (no long-lived plaintext logs)
- Rotation events emit an audit entry with prior_key_id -> new_key_id mapping
- Revoke endpoint exists and is callable by ops on POC end

Priya: Yep. We already emit audit events to the audit stream (s3 + kinesis). Revoke call is: `DELETE /v1/internal/poc-keys/<key_id>` which invalidates the token immediately and logs the revocation reason.

Casey: Can you add an automated revocation at POC end (two weeks) and a manual stop button in Console? Customer wants a hard cut-off.

Priya: I'll add a cron rule to schedule revoke at epoch-poc end date, and enable a Console button that calls the same revoke endpoint. Will also wire an on-rotate webhook to the vault so their infra gets notified without us sending token over chat.

Jordan: Pricing question from the customer — they asked whether rotating keys more frequently impacts invoicing or rate limits.

Priya: Rotation itself is control plane activity and doesn't count as inference usage. Tokens are just credentials; billing is based on inference calls. If you want to limit cost, we can set per-key rate limits and quota: `quota_per_minute` and model caps.

Casey: Nice. Any gotchas for them using SDKs?

Priya: SDKs support ephemeral tokens. Recommended pattern: SDK reads token from the vault secret mount and refreshes on 401 by re-reading the vault path. We'll provide a sample snippet for Node/Python.

devops-bot: Created provisional key record: key_id=pk_7f3b9e, project=epoch-poc, expires=1832278478, rotate_every=24h, ip_allowlist=[198.51.100.23/32,2001:db8::/64]. (Token issued to vault://redwood/pocs/epoch — token not stored in chat) :white_check_mark:

Casey: Thanks. Please add the revocation schedule and the vault webhook before I share access with Epoch.

Priya: Will do. I[0m'll post the docs and a short runbook here when finished (automation + manual). ETA: EOD tomorrow.

Lena: I'll review the runbook for compliance once posted.

Casey: Perfect — ping me when it's live and I'll hand over to the CS lead on the customer side. :thumbsup:
